subject: Conditional warm-standby SLA and acceptable data-loss window
messages:
From: Marco Ricci <marco@ledgercap.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@ledgercap.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerCap request — warm-standby SLA, acceptable RPO window

Jonas / Evelyn,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. To summarize LedgerCap's ask as we prepare procurement and legal: we need multi-region failover with a documented warm-standby activation process and a short, contractually-bound RTO window for our payments flow. Given our cost constraints, we are willing to accept a controlled RPO (data-loss) window during failover provided it is bounded and audited.

High level requirements:
- Target failover RTO: 4 hours for the payments API path (end-to-end)
- Acceptable RPO: up to 30 minutes for non-transactional features; up to 1 hour for payment settlements (we understand this is atypical but want a clear max)
- Warm-standby activation lead time: 2 hours warmup before full routing (can be shorter in emergencies)
- Runbook + post-failover audit: Redwood to provide a runbook and a post-incident data-loss reconciliation report within 5 business days

We also want to understand the SLA credit model if Redwood cannot meet RTO/RPO targets, plus any liability carveouts for cross-region replication. We've attached a short redline doc with our initial positions (ledgercap-sla-redlines.docx).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these bounds as a limited contractual exception and outline operational commitments (runbook, test cadence, reporting)? If there are costs for the guaranteed warm standby window, please provide a line-item estimate.

Thanks,
Marco
Procurement — LedgerCap

Attachments: ledgercap-sla-redlines.docx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Marco Ricci <marco@ledgercap.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LedgerCap request — warm-standby SLA, acceptable RPO window

Marco —

Appreciate the clear summary. We can support LedgerCap's intent to have a bounded warm-standby and an auditable post-failover reconciliation, but there are a few tradeoffs we should call out so procurement/legal can decide. Below is an operationally-realistic proposal we can commit to in an exception addendum: 

Proposed exception terms (summary):
- Contracted warm-standby mode (reserved capacity in standby region) with an activation RTO target of 4 hours for the payments API (measured as time to full request routing and KV cache priming).
- Contracted RPO ceilings: 1 hour for settlement-critical data; 30 minutes for non-critical datasets. These ceilings are the maximum permissible data-loss windows in the event of an immediate regional outage.
- Activation lead time: Redwood will maintain standby capacity and begin activation immediately on detection; typical warmup and staged routing will be completed within the RTO window. Manual runbook steps may be required for stateful subsystems (we will document these).
- Post-failover deliverables: runbook (pre-shared), failover timeline with timestamps, and data-loss reconciliation report delivered within 5 business days.
- Test cadence: quarterly failover rehearsals with LedgerCap participation (can be reduced to semi-annual with an uplift in monthly fee).
- SLA credits: financial credits for missed RTO are tiered (partial credit for misses <=2x target, full credit for >2x) — details to be included in the addendum.
- Liability: Redwood's exposure for data-loss during a failover is limited to service credits; any claim for direct customer losses outside credits requires mutual legal negotiation.

Costs: Maintaining warm capacity implies a reserved-cost uplift. For the scale you described in the call, ballpark uplift is ~22% on top of standard committed capacity pricing. Aditya will provide a written estimate.

We will prepare an addendum draft that maps these items into contract language and include the runbook and test plan. Does LedgerCap have a preferred window for the initial failover rehearsal (we recommend 60–90 minutes on a weekend)?

Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1-415-555-0142

Attachment: warm-standby-runbook-v1.pdf (draft)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Marco Ricci <marco@ledgercap.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LedgerCap request — warm-standby SLA, acceptable RPO window

Marco — quick note on pricing/ops tradeoffs so procurement has what you need for internal approval: 

1) Pricing: The ~22% uplift Jonas mentioned is our baseline estimate for reserved warm capacity sized to your traffic profile. If you want a stricter test cadence (monthly) or a shorter RPO ceiling (<=30m for settlement), expect a higher uplift (typically +8–12% per tightened SLA tier). We can provide a detailed line-item estimate in the next 48 hours once you confirm target concurrency and peak qps for the payments path.

2) Operational constraints: For stateful settlement queues we recommend using nearline replication to reduce RPO exposure; that adds operational complexity but materially reduces potential data-loss. We'll enumerate options in the runbook.

3) Tickets & Escalation: During any failover event, Redwood will open a high-priority incident in our portal (link below) and provide a run-of-show. If LedgerCap escalates to the Exec war room, we will loop in an SLA liaison.

Links:
- Incident portal (redwood): https://status.redwood.com/incidents/LDG-portal (internal link)
- SOW draft (for signature): https://app.redwood.com/sow/LDG-2025-1087

If you can send the peak qps and an expected transactions-per-minute metric for the payments API, I will get you a precise price delta.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marco Ricci <marco@ledgercap.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@ledgercap.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LedgerCap request — warm-standby SLA, acceptable RPO window

Jonas / Aditya —

Thanks — this directionally aligns with our needs. Procurement will review the redlines and your proposed addendum. A few quick confirmations we need before sharing internally: 

- Confirm the exact test window options (weekend 60–90 min vs. weekday 30 min) and whether the quarterly cadence is the default in the addendum.
- We accept the RPO ceilings (1h settlement / 30m non-critical) as a capped exception for the initial 12-month term subject to quarterly testing.
- We need the explicit clause that Redwood will deliver a post-failover data-loss reconciliation report within 5 business days and will preserve the audit trail for 90 days.

I'll push this to our legal and procurement today. Once we get your final pricing line items (Aditya) and the addendum/DocuSign link, we can move to signatures.

Marco Ricci
Procurement — LedgerCap

Attachments: none
